purpose: Small agent-reviewed development sanity set for evidence interpretation and benchmark plumbing. Not human ground truth, independent validation, a holdout, or financial-outcome labels.
selection_policy: Purposive selection from the existing 20 archived evidence packets: straightforward controls plus scheduling, partial rescission, and assessment/deposit distinctions. No market prices or subsequent returns consulted.
limitations: Twelve correlated document-question labels across eight documents do not estimate generalization, precision, calibration, or alpha.
Labels and the source interpretation were produced by an agent and remain subject to independent domain review.
Selection used visible documents and question definitions; future tuning against these labels makes them unsuitable as a holdout.
Underlying archived text was retrieved in 2026; the evidence manifests do not verify that this exact content version was available at historical candidate timestamps.
Legal interpretation labels do not establish market surprise, economic materiality to an issuer, or profitable execution.
excerpt_policy: Each excerpt consists of exact archived passage text joined with newline characters in the listed passage_id order; source_sha256 is inherited from its archived evidence manifest.

evidence.excerpt:
For this preliminary determination, we have calculated a de minimis countervailable
subsidy rate for each individually investigated producer/exporter of the subject merchandise.
Consistent with section 703(b)(4)(A) of the Act, we are disregarding these rates and
preliminarily determine that no countervailable subsides are being provided to
producers/exporters of the subject merchandise in Taiwan. Because the rates calculated for the
individually investigated companies are de minimis, the all others rate is also de minimis.

Memorandum, we have preliminarily determined that countervailable subsidies are not being
provided to producers and exporters of corrosion-resistant steel from Taiwan and, thus, we are
issuing a preliminary negative countervailing duty determination. Accordingly, we also
preliminarily determine that critical circumstances do not exist with regard to imports of
corrosion-resistant steel from Taiwan.

records.rationale: The current operative findings are explicitly preliminary and negative. References to critical-circumstances findings do not convert this into a final ruling.

evidence.excerpt:
Alignment With AD Final Determination
On November 10, 2015, in accordance with section 705(a)(1) of the Tariff Act of 1930,
as amended (“the Act”), United States Steel Corporation; Nucor Corporation; Steel Dynamics,
Inc.; ArcelorMittal USA, LLC; AK Steel Corp.; and, California Steel Industries (collectively,
“Petitioners”) requested an alignment of the final CVD determinations with the final AD
determinations of corrosion-resistant steel from India, Italy, the PRC, Korea, and Taiwan.
Therefore, in accordance with section 705(a)(1) of the Act and 19 CFR 351.210(b)(4)(i), we are
aligning the final CVD determinations with the final AD determinations. Consequently, the final
CVD determinations will be issued on the same date as the final AD determinations, which are
currently scheduled to be issued no later than March 5, 2016, unless postponed.3

records.rationale: This notice aligns the dates on which future final determinations will be issued. Repeated use of the word final describes scheduled future decisions, not a current merits determination.

evidence.excerpt:
SUMMARY: The Department of Commerce (Commerce) received information from U.S.
Customs and Border Protection (CBP) relating to the antidumping duty (AD) and
countervailing duty (CVD) orders on certain corrosion resistant steel products from the
Republic of Korea (Korea). Commerce is providing notice that it is opening a scope segment
in the proceeding in order to place this information on the record of the case and provide an
opportunity for interested parties to comment.

records.rationale: Commerce opens a scope segment to place CBP information on the record and invite comments. The passage does not itself resolve that scope issue.

evidence.excerpt: There is now a final court decision with respect to the Trendium Final Scope Ruling.

Therefore, Commerce is amending its scope ruling and finds that the scope of the Orders does
not cover the products addressed in the Final Scope Ruling and the Final Remand Results. The
period to appeal the CIT’s ruling expired on May 18, 2020. Because no parties appealed the
CIT’s ruling, Commerce will instruct CBP to lift suspension of liquidation of the CORE
components subject to Trendium’s Scope Request and to liquidate such entries without regard to
antidumping or countervailing duties. In addition, Commerce will instruct CBP to release any
cash deposits collected pursuant to the Orders on such entries currently awaiting liquidation.

records.rationale: Commerce amends its scope ruling following an unappealed final court decision and directs liquidation without duties plus release of deposits for the specified products.

Materiality here means narrowing the legal rate applicability, not proving material company earnings exposure.
